summary: The bill pauses the Sentinel intercontinental ballistic missile program and the related W87-1 warhead, transfers all currently available funds for those efforts to the Department of Education for Title I grants, bars new FY2026 funding for them, and requires an independent study on extending Minuteman III missiles through 2050.

scores.thoughts: The bill reallocates existing appropriated funds from the Sentinel program and W87-1 warhead to Department of Education programs rather than authorizing new spending or cutting total outlays. It does not expand or reduce overall government spending levels.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax policy, rates, credits, or revenue measures.
No provisions address healthcare policy, coverage, or funding.
No provisions relate to firearms regulation or gun rights.
No provisions address immigration, borders, or related protections.
No provisions address reproductive health or abortion access.

The bill explicitly pauses the Sentinel ICBM program, prohibits FY2026 funding for it and the W87-1 warhead, transfers current appropriations away from these programs, and directs a study on extending the older Minuteman III instead. This constitutes a clear reduction in military spending on strategic nuclear modernization.
No provisions address environmental regulations, climate policy, or energy.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net entitlements.

The bill transfers all available Sentinel and W87-1 appropriations to the Department of Education to carry out Title I-A of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, which funds public K-12 schools serving low-income students. This directly increases federal investment in public education.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policy.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
While the bill reduces spending on one defense program, the funds are transferred to education rather than used for deficit reduction, producing no net change in total outlays or debt trajectory.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
No provisions address foreign assistance or aid programs.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance.
No provisions address labor rights, union power, or workplace regulations.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
